title: Credit Card Due Reminder Notification with PII Masking
description: Verify automated due reminder notification is sent with proper card number masking and contains all required payment information.
testDescription: Test the automated notification system that sends due reminders to cardholders 7 days before payment due date, ensuring card numbers are properly masked to show only last 4 digits.
prerequisites: Active credit card account with balance due, customer notification preferences configured, notification system operational
stepsToPerform:
1. Set system date to 7 days before payment due date
2. Execute automated due reminder job
3. Verify notification generation for eligible accounts
4. Check notification content for card number masking
5. Validate delivery through configured channels (email/SMS)
6. Confirm notification logging and audit trail
expectedResult: Due reminder notification sent successfully showing card ending in XXXX (last 4 digits only), includes due date, minimum payment amount, total balance, and payment instructions
cardNumberMasking: Full card number 4532-1234-5678-9012 displayed as XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-9012
regulatoryCompliance: FDCPA compliant reminder language, no threatening or misleading content
notificationChannels: Email, SMS, mobile app notification based on customer preference
businessRules: Reminder sent 7 days before due date for accounts with balance >$25
integrationPoints: Notification service, customer preference database, card management system
dataValidation: Due date accuracy, balance amounts, customer contact information

title: Overdue Balance Alert Escalation Workflow
description: Validate overdue alert processing and account status transition when payment due date is exceeded.
testDescription: Test the escalation workflow that triggers overdue alerts and updates account delinquency status when payments are not received by due date.
prerequisites: Credit card account with unpaid balance past due date, escalation rules configured, alert notification system active
stepsToPerform:
1. Set system date to 1 day after payment due date
2. Execute overdue processing batch job
3. Verify account status change from Current to 30-days delinquent
4. Validate overdue alert generation with masked card number
5. Check late fee calculation and application
6. Confirm alert delivery and customer notification
7. Verify escalation timeline setup for next stage
expectedResult: Account status updated to 30-days overdue, late fee applied, overdue alert sent with card ending in XXXX, escalation timer initiated for 60-day processing
feeCalculation: Late fee per terms and conditions, compound interest calculation
escalationTiming: Day 1: Overdue alert, Day 30: Second notice, Day 60: Collection notice
complianceChecks: FDCPA timing requirements, state-specific collection laws
systemUpdates: Credit bureau reporting, internal risk scoring updates
alertContent: Overdue amount, late fees, payment instructions, consequences of continued non-payment

title: Collection Notification Generation and Legal Documentation
description: Test formal collection notification process for significantly delinquent accounts including legal documentation requirements.
testDescription: Verify generation and delivery of formal collection notifications for accounts 60+ days delinquent, ensuring all legal requirements and documentation standards are met.
prerequisites: Account 60+ days delinquent, collection notification templates configured, legal documentation system operational, debt validation requirements configured
stepsToPerform:
1. Identify accounts eligible for collection notification (60+ days overdue)
2. Generate formal collection notice with legal language
3. Validate card number masking in all documentation
4. Include debt validation notice as required by FDCPA
5. Generate certified mail documentation
6. Update account status to formal collection
7. Set 30-day dispute period timer
8. Log all collection activities for audit
expectedResult: Formal collection notice generated with masked card number XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-9012, includes debt validation rights, dispute instructions, sent via certified mail with tracking
legalRequirements: FDCPA Section 809 debt validation notice, state collection law compliance
documentationElements: Total debt amount, original creditor information, dispute rights, validation period
deliveryMethod: Certified mail with return receipt, email backup notification
auditTrail: Collection activity logging, document generation timestamps, delivery confirmation
riskAssessment: Credit score impact, charge-off probability calculation

title: Payment Plan Proposal Creation and Customer Negotiation Workflow
description: Validate payment plan proposal generation for customers unable to pay full overdue balance with interest rate calculations and approval workflow.
testDescription: Test the payment plan proposal system that creates structured repayment schedules with reduced interest rates for customers demonstrating hardship, including approval workflow and plan activation.
prerequisites: Delinquent account eligible for payment plan, hardship documentation received, payment plan calculation engine operational, management approval workflow configured
stepsToPerform:
1. Customer requests payment plan through customer service
2. System evaluates account eligibility based on delinquency history
3. Generate payment plan options with reduced interest rates
4. Present proposals showing payment amounts and timelines
5. Customer selects preferred plan option
6. Route to management for approval based on amount thresholds
7. Generate payment plan agreement with masked card details
8. Activate plan and set up automated payment schedule
9. Update account status to Payment Plan Active
expectedResult: Payment plan proposal created showing card XXXX-9012, reduced interest rate applied, monthly payment amounts calculated, agreement generated and activated upon approval
paymentPlanOptions: 3-month, 6-month, 12-month plans with corresponding interest rate reductions
eligibilityCriteria: Account 30+ days delinquent, no previous plan in last 12 months, balance $500-$10000
interestCalculation: Standard APR reduced by 50% during plan period, no additional late fees
approvalWorkflow: Plans under $2000 auto-approved, $2000+ require manager approval
agreementTerms: Payment dates, default consequences, plan completion benefits
systemIntegration: Payment processor setup, automatic payment scheduling, account status updates

title: Collection Agency Handoff and Legal Action Initiation Process
description: Test complete workflow for transferring severely delinquent accounts to collection agencies and initiating legal proceedings when necessary.
testDescription: Verify end-to-end process for accounts 90+ days delinquent including collection agency assignment, data transfer with PII protection, and legal action initiation for charge-off accounts.
prerequisites: Account 90+ days delinquent, collection agency contracts active, legal action criteria configured, charge-off threshold rules established, data transfer encryption operational
stepsToPerform:
1. System identifies accounts eligible for collection agency assignment (90+ days overdue)
2. Validate account meets collection agency handoff criteria
3. Generate encrypted data file with masked card numbers for agency transfer
4. Assign account to appropriate collection agency based on geography/amount
5. Transfer account data via secure FTP with audit logging
6. Update internal account status to External Collection
7. For accounts meeting legal action criteria, generate legal referral documentation
8. Route legal cases to approved law firms based on jurisdiction
9. Generate all required legal documentation with proper PII masking
10. Monitor collection agency performance and recovery rates
expectedResult: Account successfully transferred to collection agency with masked card data XXXX-9012, legal documentation generated for eligible accounts, all transfers logged and encrypted, account status updated appropriately
collectionAgencyData: Customer contact info, debt amount, payment history, account notes, masked card number
legalActionCriteria: Balance over $2500, 120+ days delinquent, unsuccessful collection agency attempts for 60+ days
dataSecurityMeasures: 256-bit encryption for data transfer, secure FTP protocols, access logging and monitoring
documentGeneration: Collection agency assignment letters, legal referral documents, court filing preparations
complianceMonitoring: FDCPA compliance tracking, agency performance metrics, legal case status updates
accountRecovery: Payment processing during external collection, account rehabilitation procedures

title: Multi-Channel Notification Delivery with Failure Recovery
description: Verify notification delivery across multiple channels with automatic retry mechanisms and fallback options when primary delivery methods fail.
testDescription: Test the notification system's ability to deliver collection communications through multiple channels (email, SMS, postal mail) with automatic retry logic and failover to alternative channels when delivery failures occur.
prerequisites: Customer with multiple contact methods configured, notification delivery system operational, retry logic configured, postal mail service integrated
stepsToPerform:
1. Configure customer with email, SMS, and postal address preferences
2. Generate overdue notification for account with balance due
3. Attempt email delivery and simulate email bounce/failure
4. Verify automatic retry attempt after configured interval
5. After max email retries exceeded, verify SMS fallback activation
6. Simulate SMS delivery failure and verify postal mail fallback
7. Confirm successful postal mail generation with tracking
8. Validate all delivery attempts logged with timestamps and status
expectedResult: Notification delivered successfully through fallback channel (postal mail) after email and SMS failures, card number masked as XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-9012 in all channels, complete audit trail of delivery attempts maintained
deliveryChannelPriority: 1st: Email, 2nd: SMS, 3rd: Postal Mail based on customer preference settings
retryConfiguration: Email: 3 attempts over 24 hours, SMS: 2 attempts over 4 hours, Postal: Single attempt with tracking
failureHandling: Bounce handling for email, carrier response codes for SMS, postal service confirmation
auditRequirements: Delivery timestamp, channel used, failure reasons, retry attempts, final delivery status
regulatoryCompliance: FDCPA delivery requirements met through multi-channel approach, proof of delivery maintained
costOptimization: Postal mail used only as last resort due to higher costs, electronic delivery preferred

title: Account Rehabilitation During Active Collection Process
description: Test account recovery workflow when customers resume payments while in active collection status, including status rollback and fee adjustments.
testDescription: Verify the account rehabilitation process that occurs when a customer makes payment during active collection, including proper status transitions, fee calculations, and collection agency notification.
prerequisites: Account in collection status (60+ days overdue), collection agency assigned, payment processing system operational, rehabilitation rules configured
stepsToPerform:
1. Account currently in External Collection status with collection agency
2. Customer makes significant payment (50%+ of overdue balance)
3. Payment processing system receives and validates payment
4. System evaluates payment against rehabilitation criteria
5. Automatically recall account from collection agency
6. Update account status from External Collection to Current
7. Calculate and reverse applicable collection fees
8. Generate rehabilitation confirmation notice with masked card number
9. Notify collection agency of account recall with reason codes
10. Update credit bureau reporting to reflect current status
expectedResult: Account status updated from External Collection to Current, collection fees reversed, confirmation sent to customer showing card XXXX-9012, collection agency notified of recall, credit bureau updated with positive payment status
rehabilitationCriteria: Payment of 50% or more of total overdue amount, account not in legal proceedings
feeReversals: Collection agency fees, legal fees if applicable, late fees per rehabilitation policy
agencyNotification: Automatic recall notice sent within 24 hours, final commission calculations processed
statusTransitions: External Collection → Payment Plan Active OR Current based on payment amount
creditBureauUpdates: Current payment status reported, delinquency status updated within regulatory timeframes
customerCommunication: Rehabilitation welcome letter, updated payment terms, account restoration confirmation

title: Cross-System Integration Failure Recovery and Data Consistency
description: Validate system behavior and data consistency when integration failures occur between collection systems, payment processors, and external agencies.
testDescription: Test the system's ability to maintain data consistency and recover gracefully when integration points fail between internal collection systems, payment processors, and external collection agencies.
prerequisites: Multi-system architecture operational, integration monitoring enabled, error handling procedures configured, data reconciliation processes active
stepsToPerform:
1. Initiate collection agency data transfer for delinquent accounts
2. Simulate network failure during data transmission midway through process
3. Verify partial data rollback and transaction integrity maintenance
4. Restart integration process with proper error recovery
5. Validate no duplicate accounts sent to collection agency
6. Simulate payment processor timeout during customer payment
7. Verify payment status remains pending until confirmation received
8. Test collection agency status update failure scenario
9. Confirm internal systems maintain accurate account status
10. Execute end-of-day reconciliation to identify and resolve discrepancies
expectedResult: System maintains data integrity during failures, no duplicate collection assignments, payment statuses accurate, all discrepancies identified and resolved through reconciliation, masked card numbers XXXX-9012 consistent across all systems
integrationPoints: Collection agency API, payment processor gateway, credit bureau reporting, notification service
failureScenarios: Network timeouts, API service unavailability, data corruption, authentication failures
errorRecoveryMethods: Transaction rollback, retry with exponential backoff, manual intervention queues
dataConsistencyChecks: Account status synchronization, payment amount matching, collection assignment validation
monitoringAlerts: Integration failure notifications, data mismatch alerts, SLA violation warnings
reconciliationProcess: Daily batch reconciliation, exception reporting, automated correction procedures

title: Regulatory Compliance Validation for FDCPA Requirements
description: Comprehensive testing of Fair Debt Collection Practices Act compliance across all collection communications and processes.
testDescription: Validate complete FDCPA compliance throughout collection lifecycle including required disclosures, prohibited practices, timing restrictions, and customer rights protection.
prerequisites: FDCPA compliance rules configured, legal language templates approved, timing restrictions implemented, dispute handling procedures active
stepsToPerform:
1. Generate initial collection notice and verify required FDCPA disclosures present
2. Validate debt validation notice includes all required elements per Section 809
3. Test 30-day dispute period enforcement and validation rights
4. Verify prohibited language is blocked from all communications
5. Test timing restrictions for contact attempts (8am-9pm local time)
6. Validate cease communication requests are honored immediately
7. Test third-party contact restrictions and privacy protections
8. Verify legal action threats only appear when action is intended
9. Validate all communications include proper identification of collection entity
10. Test customer rights explanations in all notices with masked card data
expectedResult: All collection communications fully FDCPA compliant, required disclosures present, prohibited practices blocked, customer rights protected, card numbers properly masked as XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-9012 throughout process
fdcpaDisclosures: Debt validation rights, dispute period, collection entity identification, original creditor information
prohibitedPractices: Harassment, false statements, unfair practices, threatening illegal action
timingRestrictions: Contact hours 8am-9pm local time, frequency limits, workplace contact restrictions
disputeHandling: 30-day validation period, debt verification requirements, dispute investigation process
customerRights: Cease communication requests, attorney representation, dispute rights, validation requests
auditCompliance: Regulatory audit trail, compliance scoring, violation prevention controls

title: Dynamic Collection Strategy Assignment Based on Customer Segmentation
description: Test intelligent collection strategy assignment system that determines optimal collection approach based on customer risk profile, payment history, and demographic factors.
testDescription: Verify the dynamic collection strategy engine that analyzes customer data to assign appropriate collection approaches ranging from soft reminder campaigns to aggressive collection tactics based on risk scoring and segmentation.
prerequisites: Customer segmentation engine operational, risk scoring models active, collection strategy templates configured, machine learning algorithms trained
stepsToPerform:
1. Customer account becomes 30 days overdue triggering strategy assignment
2. System analyzes customer payment history over last 24 months
3. Risk scoring engine calculates probability of payment recovery
4. Demographic and behavioral data incorporated into segmentation model
5. System assigns collection strategy: Soft, Standard, or Aggressive approach
6. Strategy determines notification frequency, channel preference, and escalation timing
7. High-value customers assigned to specialized retention team
8. Low-balance accounts routed to automated collection workflows
9. Strategy effectiveness tracked and models updated based on outcomes
10. Manual strategy override capability tested for special circumstances
expectedResult: Customer assigned to appropriate collection strategy based on risk profile, collection approach optimized for recovery probability, notifications customized per strategy with masked card XXXX-9012, strategy performance tracked for continuous improvement
segmentationFactors: Payment history, account age, balance amount, customer tenure, previous collection response
collectionStrategies: Soft: Gentle reminders, extended payment terms; Standard: Regular escalation; Aggressive: Frequent contact, immediate escalation
riskScoringElements: Credit score, payment patterns, demographic factors, external credit data
strategyOptimization: A/B testing of approaches, machine learning model updates, ROI tracking
specialHandling: VIP customer protection, hardship consideration, legal restriction compliance
performanceMetrics: Recovery rate by strategy, cost per dollar collected, customer satisfaction impact

title: Batch Payment Processing During Collection Cycle with Account Status Updates
description: Verify batch payment processing capabilities during active collection cycles including partial payments, overpayments, and real-time account status synchronization across all systems.
testDescription: Test the batch payment processing system's ability to handle multiple payment types during collection cycles while maintaining accurate account balances and triggering appropriate status changes.
prerequisites: Multiple accounts in various collection stages, batch payment processing system operational, real-time balance calculation engine active, account status update rules configured
stepsToPerform:
1. Set up accounts in different collection stages (30-day, 60-day, 90-day overdue)
2. Process batch containing partial payments, full payments, and overpayments
3. Verify real-time balance updates and interest calculations
4. Validate automatic account status transitions based on payment amounts
5. Test overpayment handling and credit balance creation
6. Confirm collection agency notifications for paid accounts
7. Verify payment allocation priority (fees, interest, principal)
8. Test batch processing failure scenarios and rollback procedures
9. Validate payment confirmation generation with masked card numbers
10. Confirm credit bureau reporting updates for positive payment activity
expectedResult: All payments processed accurately with proper balance updates, account statuses automatically updated based on payment amounts, overpayments create credit balances, collection agencies notified of account changes, confirmations sent showing card XXXX-9012
paymentAllocationRules: Priority order: Collection fees, late fees, accrued interest, principal balance
statusTransitionLogic: Partial payment >25% moves to payment plan consideration, >75% returns to current status
overpaymentHandling: Credit balance created, automatic refund processing for amounts >$50
batchProcessingLimits: Maximum 10000 transactions per batch, 2-hour processing window
failureRecovery: Transaction-level rollback, error logging, manual intervention queue
regulatoryReporting: Positive payment activity reported to credit bureaus within 30 days

title: Customer Communication Preference Management and Opt-Out Compliance
description: Test comprehensive customer communication preference system including opt-out requests, channel preferences, and legal compliance for communication restrictions.
testDescription: Validate the customer communication preference management system that allows customers to control how and when they receive collection communications while maintaining regulatory compliance requirements.
prerequisites: Customer preference database operational, opt-out processing system active, legal compliance rules configured, communication channel management system functional
stepsToPerform:
1. Customer updates communication preferences to email-only notifications
2. System validates preference changes and updates all notification rules
3. Test opt-out request for specific communication types (marketing vs collections)
4. Verify legal collection communications continue despite marketing opt-out
5. Test complete communication cease request and immediate enforcement
6. Validate attorney representation notification and communication restrictions
7. Test time-based communication preferences (work hours only)
8. Verify third-party contact restrictions are enforced
9. Test preference inheritance for joint account holders
10. Validate emergency communication overrides for critical account status changes
expectedResult: Customer preferences accurately applied to all communications, opt-out requests immediately enforced, legal collection notices continue as required, attorney representation flags block direct communication, preferences synchronized across all systems
communicationTypes: Due reminders, overdue alerts, collection notices, payment confirmations, account updates
optOutCategories: Marketing communications, promotional offers, general account updates, collection communications
legalExceptions: Legally required collection notices, court documents, regulatory communications cannot be opted out
channelOptions: Email, SMS, phone calls, postal mail, mobile app notifications
timingPreferences: Business hours only, weekend exclusions, time zone considerations
complianceEnforcement: FDCPA cease communication requirements, attorney representation protocols, TCPA compliance for automated calls

title: Collection Fee Calculation and Reversal Workflow Validation
description: Verify accurate calculation, application, and reversal of collection-related fees including late fees, collection agency fees, and legal costs throughout the collection lifecycle.
testDescription: Test the fee calculation engine that applies various collection-related charges and handles fee reversals when accounts are rehabilitated or when fees are disputed and found invalid.
prerequisites: Fee calculation engine operational, fee structure tables configured, reversal workflow active, dispute handling system functional, accounting system integration operational
stepsToPerform:
1. Account enters 30-day overdue status triggering late fee calculation
2. Verify late fee application based on account terms and state regulations
3. Account progresses to collection agency assignment adding agency fees
4. Test compound interest calculation on overdue balances including fees
5. Customer disputes collection agency fee and fee review process initiated
6. Invalid fee identified and automatic reversal processing triggered
7. Test fee waiver approvals for customer retention purposes
8. Verify accounting system synchronization for all fee transactions
9. Test fee cap enforcement per state regulations and account terms
10. Validate fee disclosure requirements in all customer communications
expectedResult: All fees calculated accurately per account terms and regulations, fee reversals processed correctly with accounting entries, disputed fees reviewed and resolved appropriately, fee disclosures included in communications with masked card XXXX-9012
feeTypes: Late payment fees, over-limit fees, collection agency fees, legal fees, returned payment fees
calculationRules: Percentage-based and flat fee structures, minimum and maximum fee limits, state regulation compliance
reversalTriggers: Account rehabilitation, successful disputes, management waiver approvals, regulatory violations
disputeProcess: Fee review workflow, documentation requirements, resolution timeframes, customer notification
accountingIntegration: Real-time GL posting, fee accrual tracking, revenue recognition, audit trail maintenance
regulatoryCompliance: State fee limitation laws, FDCPA fee disclosure requirements, Truth in Lending Act compliance

title: Legal Documentation Generation and Court Filing Preparation
description: Test comprehensive legal documentation system for court filing preparation including judgment documentation, asset verification, and legal fee calculations with proper PII protection.
testDescription: Verify the legal documentation generation system that creates court-ready documents for debt collection litigation including proper formatting, required disclosures, and complete case documentation.
prerequisites: Legal documentation templates configured, court filing system integration active, asset verification system operational, legal fee calculation engine functional, document security protocols implemented
stepsToPerform:
1. Account meets legal action criteria (120+ days overdue, $2500+ balance)
2. System generates preliminary legal case documentation
3. Asset verification process initiated through integrated services
4. Legal fee calculations performed including court costs and attorney fees
5. Court filing documents generated with proper formatting and requirements
6. Validate all PII masking in legal documents showing only last 4 card digits
7. Test document routing to appropriate law firm based on jurisdiction
8. Verify legal case tracking and milestone management
9. Test judgment documentation and post-judgment collection procedures
10. Validate legal document storage and retrieval with security controls
expectedResult: Complete legal documentation package generated with proper formatting, PII properly masked showing card XXXX-9012, documents routed to correct jurisdiction, legal case tracking initiated, all security protocols enforced
documentTypes: Complaint filing, affidavit of debt, account statements, payment history, judgment documentation
jurisdictionRules: State-specific court requirements, filing fee schedules, service of process procedures
assetVerification: Bank account searches, employment verification, property ownership checks, credit report analysis
legalFeeCalculation: Court filing fees, attorney fees, service costs, post-judgment collection costs
securityProtocols: Document encryption, access logging, retention policies, disposal procedures
caseManagement: Milestone tracking, hearing schedules, judgment enforcement, settlement negotiations

title: Cross-Border Collection Process for International Cardholders
description: Validate collection processes for international credit card holders including currency conversion, international notification delivery, and compliance with foreign debt collection regulations.
testDescription: Test the international collection system that handles cross-border debt collection including multi-currency processing, international delivery methods, and compliance with various national debt collection laws.
prerequisites: International collection system operational, currency conversion engine active, international notification delivery services configured, foreign regulatory compliance rules implemented, translation services available
stepsToPerform:
1. International customer account becomes overdue with balance in foreign currency
2. System converts overdue amounts to customer's local currency for notifications
3. Generate collection notices in customer's preferred language with proper translation
4. Validate international delivery methods (international mail, email, SMS)
5. Test compliance with foreign debt collection laws and restrictions
6. Verify currency fluctuation impact on payment amounts and fees
7. Test international payment processing and currency conversion fees
8. Validate time zone considerations for communication timing restrictions
9. Test cross-border legal action limitations and procedures
10. Verify compliance reporting to multiple regulatory jurisdictions
expectedResult: International collection notices delivered successfully in local currency and language, foreign regulatory compliance maintained, payment processing handles currency conversion accurately, card numbers masked as XXXX-9012 in all languages
currencyConversion: Real-time exchange rates, conversion fee calculations, currency fluctuation handling
languageSupport: Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Japanese translation capabilities
internationalDelivery: International postal service integration, global SMS gateway, email localization
regulatoryCompliance: GDPR compliance for EU customers, local debt collection laws, data residency requirements
paymentProcessing: Multi-currency payment acceptance, foreign exchange fees, international bank transfers
legalRestrictions: Countries with collection prohibitions, diplomatic immunity considerations, treaty obligations
